newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks climb to new highs at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks climb to new highs at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open on Monday as stocks rose nearly across the board. * 5.1 million shares traded worth C$57.1 million.
Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open on Monday as issues rose nearly across the board.
Twelve of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes climbed at the open, led by communications, which gained 98.72 points or 0.83 percent to 12013.74.
Traders said interest in CanWest Global Communications Corp and Thomson Corp helped fuel the sector's rise but early volumes were light.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index rose 13.38 points to 6639.78 in turnover of 5.1 million shares.
Total trading value was C$57.1 million. Advances outpaced declines 203 to 178, while 196 issues traded flat.

"CanWest Global is up 0.60...they reported excellent numbers on Friday, in line with street expectations, and they're talking about doing all kinds of good things. So that one continues to roll," one trader said.

The Winnipeg-based television broadcaster on Friday reported third-quarter per share earnings of C$0.25, up from C$0.18 in the same period a year ago. CanWest shares rose 0.95 to 23.90 in healthy trading on Friday.
Gold stocks lost some ground in early trade as Comex prices failed to rebound further in New York after last week's bounce off 12-year lows.
One trader said major Canadian gold producers had likely rallied as far as possible and might now face selling.

"Barrick (Gold Corp ) and Placer (Dome Inc) are probably up to where they could run into resistance at any time, because I don't think the down(trend) is (over) so, for traders you maybe want to be very nimble and want to be taking profits at this point," the trader said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shares in Semi-Tech Corp rose 1.15 to 4.75 in early trade before settling to 4.50 in heavy volume after U.S. publicity sparked investor interest.
"Apparently it was written up in either Barrons or one of the other financial journals in the U.S. as just being undervalued...so it had a gap opening and has had a bit of a run," one trader said.
